title: A UI kit separable from decade
body:
decade's UI kit becomes its own crate in this workspace, under the working name `decade-ui`. The kit serves programs that look and behave like decade. Their chrome sits on a grid of monospace cells, their panes sit in a split tree with tabs and bars, and their overlays are boxed lists. A toolkit for any 2D UI, such as a game HUD, is out of scope. egui and Dear ImGui already fill that role.

The first program besides decade's server to run the kit is the remote viewer in decade-e3a784. That viewer draws the chrome itself, and on macOS it has no smithay.

## What the kit holds

- the cell grid, `Rgba` and the theme colours
- `Scene` and its shapes
- fonts, and text rasterized to CPU bitmaps
- the overlay widgets: boxed lists, rows, the cursor, key caps, hints, the text field, the confirm dialog and the context menu widget
- panes: the split tree, tabs, pane bars, drop zones, zoom, hit testing, and the drag state machine that resizes, moves and focuses panes

## What stays out

- Windows, the event loop, Wayland and the GPU. Each program writes a painter that turns a `Scene` and text bitmaps into draws. decade keeps its GLES `Paint` and its texture cache. The kit ships no painter until the macOS viewer exists.
- What a pane shows. A pane tab holds an opaque content id, and the kit leaves a `Shape::Content { id, rect }` placeholder for it.
- The program's verbs. Widgets and pane input return actions of the program's own type.
- decade's own widgets: the top bar, the sidebar, the palette, the picker and the settings panel. They stay in the `decade` crate, in a module that imports no smithay, so a macOS build of the viewer compiles them without the server.

## Decided

Jack signed off this design on 2026-11-19.

- A program adds tags and bar buttons to a pane as data on the pane. Each button carries the program's own action, and the kit returns that action on a click. decade fills these from its scratch and screenshot state. This answers the note of 2026-11-11.
- The kit owns pane input.
- Crate and type names are settled after the crate is built.

The design must not change how decade owns and manages Wayland windows.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/7403d304
notes.text: The screenshot mode from d73fd69 lives in the kit's pane code in src/server/panes.rs: Pane::screenshots, the left outline tag and its flash, and a Ctrl bar button. The kit is meant to hold nothing decade-specific, so the split needs a way for the application to add its own per-pane modes, tags and bar buttons. The scratch pane tag and button are in the same position.
